title: Defibrillators
banner: DRAFT, NOT clinically reviewed. Device-neutral educational specification; never imported, published or shown to learners.

parameters.name: Rhythm display
parameters.explanation: The rhythm display supports trained rhythm assessment. Check the clinical state, distinguish arrest from a rhythm with a pulse, and do not decide to shock from an isolated monitor label.

parameters.name: Energy setting
parameters.explanation: The energy selected for a shock is distinct from rhythm assessment and charge status. The appropriate selection depends on the defibrillator waveform and resuscitation protocol; only authorised trained staff make that selection.

parameters.name: Charge state
parameters.explanation: Indicates the device's preparation for shock delivery, not a clinical instruction to deliver a shock. During manual CPR the trained team minimizes interruptions, continues compressions while charging where appropriate, clears contact before shock and follows device-specific safety procedures.

safety_concepts.text: Perform and call a safety check so nobody touches the patient or bed at the moment of shock; do not defibrillate during manual chest compressions, even with gloves.
Pads are preferred over paddles when available; if paddles are used apply firm force and good contact to limit arcing.
Keep the pre-shock pause as short as possible: compressions continue while the defibrillator charges; a coordinated team can complete manual defibrillation with under 5 seconds of interruption.

In adult cardiac arrest, unsynchronised defibrillation is used for ventricular fibrillation or pulseless ventricular tachycardia, not asystole or pulseless electrical activity. Synchronized cardioversion for indicated tachyarrhythmias with a pulse is a distinct clinician-led procedure; follow current resuscitation training and the device instructions.

escalation_concepts.text: Call for help early; follow the oxygen-safety steps in unit policy during defibrillation.
